expected_output.reasoning: The investigation correctly identifies that worker-a's data disk (<volume-id>, gp3 at 125 MiB/s) is throughput-capped, causing jobs to take ~3x longer (~31-33s vs ~10.8s) and limiting worker-a's completion rate, while worker-b's identical setup but with a 500 MiB/s disk performs normally. It correctly rules out CPU (low utilization on both), instance-level EBS bandwidth (EBSByteBalance% at 99%), and IOPS (both well under 3,000 provisioned) as bottlenecks, matching the expected root cause's exclusion criteria. The investigation traces this to the CloudFormation stack parameter WorkerADataDiskMiBps=125 vs WorkerBDataDiskMiBps=500, which aligns with 'the included 125 MiB/s throughput' in the expected root cause. The combined capacity shortfall (~3,540/h vs ~4,320/h sent) causing backlog growth matches the expected narrative of ~60 jobs/min vs ~72 jobs/min. The investigation also correctly notes the recommended fix (raise worker-a's throughput to 500 MiB/s) matches the expected fix (raise to at least ~400 MiB/s). All key identifying details (service, volume IDs, throughput caps, timing, causal chain) align closely with the expected root cause.
